tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Estimates on derivatives] ↗ thm:heat-equation-smoothness 1. ch2:2.3-thm-9\group Heat Equation

For every $k,l\in \N $ there is $C_{kl}$ such that \[ \max _{C(x,t;r/2)}|D_x^kD_t^lu| \le \frac{C_{kl}}{r^{k+2l+n+2}} \| u\| _{L^1(C(x,t;r))} \] whenever $C(x,t;r)\subset U_T$ and $u$ solves the heat equation.
Proof

\sketch On the unit cylinder, the smooth-kernel representation from the regularity proof yields

\[ |D_x^kD_t^lu|\le C_{kl}\| u\| _{L^1(C(1))} \]

on the half cylinder. For $C(r)$, apply this to $v(x,t)=u(rx,r^2t)$. Since $D_x^kD_t^lv=r^{k+2l}(D_x^kD_t^lu)(rx,r^2t)$ and $\| v\| _{L^1(C(1))}=r^{-n-2}\| u\| _{L^1(C(r))}$, the stated exponent follows.

□
